description:
Deferrals recorded by the P3/P4 port agents, each documented in-file at the point
it applies. Collected here so they are not lost:

- Isotropic cracking (nCracks / sliceMapper / lhgr crack-softening) on the UO2,
  MOX and SCK-CEN Young's-modulus and UO2/MOX Poisson models. Needs damage-model
  state and a slice mapper, so not a pure function of MaterialState. All variants
  currently return the upstream nominal value.
- Transversely isotropic PyC: upstream itself returns the isotropic average
  (E_r + 2 E_t)/3 with a TODO. Real anisotropy needs a direction-dependent
  modulus in the mechanics layer.
- PARFUMEPyC thermal-expansion spherical-to-Cartesian tensor rotation: upstream
  does it in correct() using mesh_.C()[cellI]; it is a mesh operation and belongs
  in the mechanics assembly.
- swellingPARFUMEBuffer / swellingPARFUMEPyC: they integrate eps += rate*flux*dt,
  so they need fast flux and the timestep, plus a 2-D table interpolator in
  temperature x Bacon Anisotropy Factor and a 1-D one in coating density.
- burnupLassmann / burnupLassmannFBR (~75 KB): TUBRNP-style radial depletion
  solving a reduced Bateman chain for ~14 nuclides plus radial power
  reconstruction. That is neutronics and needs a flux solution.
- Axial-shape half of timeDependentAxialProfile: needs a mesh, pin direction and
  the profiles/ library.
- Relocation recovery (recoveryFraction/relaxRecovery), slice averaging, the
  max/min ratchets and the sensitivity scaling: history/mesh/contact logic.
- SCIANTIX physics: returns NotImplemented, never a silent zero. Separate
  MIT-licensed code with its own licence-provenance and V&V obligations.

Most of these are blocked on the same two things: the damage model and the
slice mapper. Worth sequencing them behind those rather than picking them off.
title: offbeat: deferred sub-models from the P3/P4 port (cracking, PyC anisotropy, PARFUME swelling, Lassmann burnup, relocation recovery)

description: GH issue #35 comment 2026-09-01 05:22: 'opening new pdfs, kovan should ask if you want to ingest it. Give an option/checkbox to auto-ingest opened pdfs otherwise, ask users when users open pdf viewer.' When FileDialogTarget::Pdf is picked, a Kovan root is open, and the path is not already under root.open_sources_dir()/restricted_sources_dir() (i.e. not already an ingested paper's stored source -- ingest.rs's own storage convention), either silently run WikiState::begin_ingest (if an 'always auto-ingest' preference is on) or show a small Ingest/Skip prompt that also offers to turn that preference on.

notes.content: Implemented in commit 91cb7594 (develop). See commit message / issue #35 comment for details.

title: PDF Reader: prompt to ingest an externally opened PDF, with an auto-ingest checkbox

design:
Child of the multi-thermo flowsheet epic (bn op-186o).


Define what the stream owns as **physical, conserved state**, separate from any
package's interpretation of it.

Must preserve: mass inventory; molar inventory where defined; **elemental
inventory**; pressure; energy/enthalpy; flow; provenance; representation
metadata.

## The subtle requirement

**Temperature must not be treated as automatically invariant across a package
transition.** Two packages can assign different enthalpies to the same
(T, P, composition), so a transition cannot preserve T *and* P *and* H *and*
composition simultaneously when the packages disagree. The canonical state must
be expressible in a way that makes that trade explicit rather than hiding it.

Elemental inventory is the anchor: it is the one thing every package must
agree on, and it is what makes conservation checkable independently of any
package.


## Constraints

Mature-crate refactor: preserve public constructors, deprecate rather than remove, regression tests before semantic changes. Do not implement AGR/Claus/the refinery here. `develop` only, no push to `main`.
title: MultiThermo: Canonical stream-state definition
